fatal_errors: The proposed grain-boundary segregation and precipitation mechanism merely restates the conventional-alloy expectation rather than testing the distinct phase-boundary and ordering mechanism.
The intervention of 800°C for 100 hours misses the critical intermediate-temperature aging window and does not compare the embrittling 600°C condition with ductility recovery near 750°C.
The predicted monotonic 20% toughness loss conflicts with the observed non-monotonic ductile-brittle-ductile transition.
The falsification threshold is based on arbitrary toughness percentages and cannot establish whether grain-boundary precipitation caused any degradation.
explanation: The response addresses thermal embrittlement only at a generic level. It does not reconstruct the relevant as-cast FCC+B2 AlCoCrFeNi2.1 microstructure, enhanced L12 ordering, jagged FCC/B2 phase boundaries, elevated APBE, restricted cross-slip, planar slip, or crack initiation at phase-boundary tips. Its broad service boundaries are unsupported, and it omits controlled aging across the 550–750°C window. Although TEM/STEM and mechanical testing could contribute to a valid experiment, the proposed design lacks measurements of ordering, phase-boundary morphology, dislocation pile-ups, and impurity segregation needed to discriminate the hypotheses. A decisive test would correlate minimum ductility near 600°C with maximal L12 ordering and jagged phase boundaries, then show recovery near 750°C as ordering decreases and ductile transition zones form; observation of grain-boundary impurity segregation and brittle precipitates instead would falsify the target mechanism.
